topic: Environmental cumulant-flag identification under simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise shifts. Fix d, E>=d+2 and Rmax, balanced environment sample shares, a three-variable acyclic linear SEM U=epsilon_u, T=alpha U+epsilon_t, Y=beta T+gamma U+epsilon_y, bounded coefficients/moments, independent centered entire-mgf noises, invariant alpha,beta,gamma,epsilon_y, and latent cumulant-shift vectors u_r in one unknown d-plane A spanned with a fixed singular gap by observed treatment contrasts c_2,...,c_{d+1}. Work on D_rho=B union N_rho: B contains every bounded law whose first projected breakout r*=min{r>=d+2:Q_A c_r!=0} is at most Rmax; N_rho contains global no-breakout laws only when their exact source-swapped partners satisfy all bounds with rho slack. Prove beta is identified on B by beta=<Q_Ac_r*,Q_Am_r*>/||Q_Ac_r*||^2 and is nonidentified on N_rho via the legal source swap; prove E>=d+2 is sharp. For each r<=Rmax construct legal unequal-beta Poisson-Gaussian laws agreeing in all mixed moments below r. On first-breakout shells ||Q_Ac_r|| in [lambda_n,2lambda_n], prove minimax squared error min{B^2,1/(n lambda_n^2)}, shortest uniformly honest interval length min{B,1/(sqrt(n)lambda_n)}, and consistency iff sqrt(n)lambda_n diverges, attained by cumulant-SVD quotient GMM and Anderson-Rubin inversion. Consumer: Sachs et al. multi-environment protein signaling. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Compound-Poisson rate perturbations with binomial alternating coefficients annihilate every cumulant below r and create breakout epsilon r!, yielding legal unequal-effect matched-order twins. A covariance-preserving Gaussian/Hermite family keeps the complete baseline observed law fixed and gives full-observation KL at most C n lambda^2 times squared effect separation. Exact checks reproduce the three-environment root beta=2, swap legality, low-order moment equality, and the sharp 1-2alpha honest-length factor; calibration-rank loss, delayed breakouts, and singular influence covariance were tested. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the uniform estimated-A cumulant influence expansion and triangular-array Gaussian approximation under fixed 2Rmax+delta moments, including singular influence covariance. EARLY KILL TEST: For d=1,E=3,r=3 and beta in [1.9,2.3], certify positivity and fixed lambda of the Gaussian/Hermite sources, uniformly bound the likelihood derivative integral, and reproduce the estimated-A correction; stop if same-model legality or the KL bound fails. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_cumulant_flag_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can three or more environments restore point identification of a treatment effect under simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise shifts when latent cumulant-shift vectors occupy an unknown low-rank subspace and a finite-order treatment contrast exits that subspace?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves nonidentification when latent and treatment noises both vary across two environments and leaves identification from more than two environments for future work.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Sina Akbari, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: BACKSHIFT shows that additional environments can create identifying rank information: covariance differences identify its linear cyclic system almost surely when at least three settings are available.
source_refs.author: Dominik Rothenhäusler, Christina Heinze, Jonas Peters, Nicolai Meinshausen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-environment source swap of Kivva et al. establishes failure under simultaneous noise changes but does not use joint restrictions across several environments. BACKSHIFT confirms that environment multiplicity can produce rank information, but only through covariance differences and a different shift model. What is missing is an all-orders decomposition of environment-indexed cumulant contrasts into an unknown latent-shift plane and a treatment-noise component, together with a same-model source swap when no component leaves that plane.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An identifiable-versus-nonidentifiable frontier indexed by latent-shift rank, environment count, and first breakout order, with an explicit projected-cumulant recovery functional and observationally equivalent unequal-effect witnesses on the no-breakout region.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation and problem formulation: heterogeneous environments help under a single changing mechanism, simultaneous shifts defeat two-environment identification, and additional environments are the stated next question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent confounding blocks ordinary effect identification -> higher-order environmental moments reveal a changing mechanism -> simultaneous latent and treatment shifts create a two-environment ambiguity -> joint low-rank geometry across additional environments may resolve it

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its mixed-cumulant ratio algebra and explicit source-swapping construction, replacing a single environment difference by projection orthogonal to an environment-shift subspace.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It studies the same three-variable confounded SEM and supplies both the higher-order identifying equations and the simultaneous-shift obstruction.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over environmental GMM stacking, optimal weighting, and sandwich influence calculations after replacing covariance moments with projected cumulant moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sample analogue of the proposed recovery functional is an overidentified environmental moment system.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the minimax estimation risk and shortest uniformly honest confidence length when the first projected cumulant breakout is local to zero and the latent-shift subspace is estimated from the same samples, including singular influence covariance?

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies population identification formulas and simulation estimators but no limit law, confidence procedure, minimax rate, or weak-breakout analysis.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Sina Akbari, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Causal Dantzig derives regular low-dimensional intervals under additive interventions and notes variance inflation from weak interventions, but assumes a fixed invertible population contrast.
source_refs.author: Dominik Rothenhäusler, Peter Bühlmann, Nicolai Meinshausen

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs uniformly size-correct Anderson–Rubin and conditional QLR tests for weakly identified moment models while allowing singular moment covariance.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic weak-GMM theory starts from a supplied moment map. Here the moment is generated by estimating a spectral projector from lower-order cumulant contrasts and may be chosen after locating the first breakout. Near zero breakout the quotient is nonregular, projector estimation contributes a first-order correction, and rank loss can make the influence covariance exactly singular. None of the closest results combines this generated spectral nuisance, high-order cumulants, weak denominator, and singular covariance under a fixed moment envelope.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform triangular-array influence expansion and Gaussian approximation for the cumulant-SVD quotient, matching minimax squared-error and honest-length bounds in the breakout magnitude, and Anderson–Rubin inversion with valid coverage through zero and singular covariance.

writing_exemplar.why: Its population formulas and empirical algorithms make weak-signal inference the natural next statistical rung.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Higher-order environmental moments identify the effect in favorable shift regimes -> empirical cumulants yield a quotient estimator -> small distinguishing cumulants destabilize that quotient -> develop rate-optimal and uniformly valid weak-breakout inference

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt singularity-robust projection and null-imposed Anderson–Rubin testing, including uniform size control under drifting identification strength.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cumulant moment can be unidentified at zero breakout and can have singular covariance, precisely the paired failures treated by this method.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its environmental GMM weighting and sandwich expansion as the regular-regime base, then add the estimated-projector influence term.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both procedures aggregate invariant causal moments across heterogeneous environments with hidden confounding.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the first identifying cumulant order be selected from data while retaining uniformly valid effect inference over laws with delayed, vanishing, or absent breakouts up to a fixed maximum order?

source_refs.claim: Its algorithms use a population loop that finds the smallest moment order at which environments differ, without a sampling-theoretic stopping rule or post-selection coverage result.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Sina Akbari, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: The paper proves Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of correlated sums and applies them to adaptive specification testing.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Kengo Kato

open_problems.why_unsolved: A sample cannot uniformly distinguish an exactly zero lower-order contrast from a local nonzero one, and selecting the first rejected order changes the distribution of the ensuing quotient. Standard maximum-statistic calibration does not directly resolve this because projected cumulants at all orders share an estimated subspace, have higher-order influence polynomials, and meet on a singular intersection under global no-breakout.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A data-driven stopping and inversion procedure over cumulant orders with uniform familywise coverage and oracle-rate adaptation on separated breakout shells, or a matching impossibility theorem quantifying the unavoidable adaptation loss.

writing_exemplar.why: Its smallest-differing-order loop is the exact population formulation that must become an honest statistical procedure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Non-Gaussian shifts may first appear at an unknown order -> population identification searches until a contrast appears -> samples cannot separate exact zeros from local alternatives for free -> construct honest adaptive order selection and effect inference

method_exemplars.technique: Retain its first-differing-order identification logic while rewriting every candidate order as a null moment indexed by the causal effect.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired procedure is the finite-sample counterpart of its population search loop.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Gaussian comparison, anti-concentration, and multiplier-bootstrap control for the maximum across correlated candidate cumulant orders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Order selection is governed by the maximum of correlated empirical moment contrasts and therefore requires simultaneous rather than pointwise calibration.

open_problems.open_problem: Do higher-order environmental cumulant flags identify a selected equilibrium intervention response in stable linear cyclic systems with latent confounding when latent-source and endogenous-node noises shift simultaneously?

source_refs.claim: BACKSHIFT identifies linear cyclic systems with latent variables from covariance differences under unknown shift interventions, but uses only second moments and a more restrictive shift structure.
source_refs.author: Dominik Rothenhäusler, Christina Heinze, Jonas Peters, Nicolai Meinshausen

source_refs.claim: Higher-order moments recover a confounded treatment effect in an acyclic three-variable SEM under one changing mechanism, while simultaneous latent and treatment shifts cause two-environment nonidentification.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Sina Akbari, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: In its Sachs analysis, JCI emphasizes strong feedback, likely latent confounding, and interventions of uncertain specificity in protein signaling.
source_refs.author: Joris M. Mooij, Sara Magliacane, Tom Claassen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature contains covariance-based cyclic identification and higher-cumulant acyclic effect identification, but the scan found no result combining cyclic equilibrium propagation with simultaneous latent and node-noise changes. The triangular source-to-observable map used in the acyclic proof must be replaced by the resolvent of the cyclic coefficient matrix, while any nonidentification swap must preserve stability and all equilibrium distributions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient cumulant-rank characterization and explicit recovery functional for an equilibrium intervention response, accompanied by stable observationally equivalent cyclic models with unequal responses when the characterization fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It offers the closest destination framing around equilibrium observations, feedback, latent variables, unknown shifts, and environment-count identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Feedback systems defeat acyclic discovery -> equilibrium shifts create cross-environment contrasts -> covariance diagonalization identifies under restrictive shifts -> higher-order cumulant geometry may handle simultaneous latent and endogenous-noise changes

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over equilibrium reduced-form differencing and joint diagonalization through the resolvent of a stable cyclic coefficient matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how unknown shifts identify cyclic structure despite latent variables.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace covariance-only contrasts by mixed higher-cumulant identities and adapt the simultaneous-noise source-swap obstruction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the non-Gaussian effect-identification machinery absent from BACKSHIFT.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt semiparametric pseudo-likelihood consistency and asymptotic-distribution arguments for non-Gaussian mixing matrices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A stable cyclic SEM observed at equilibrium creates a non-Gaussian mixing-matrix inference problem analogous to structural VAR identification.

open_problems.open_problem: How much of a protein-signaling causal effect remains identified when exact low-rank cumulant-shift and acyclicity assumptions are relaxed by bounded off-target intervention, latent-shift, and feedback misspecification?

source_refs.claim: JCI reports that Sachs interventions are mostly imperfect and of uncertain specificity, while the signaling network likely contains latent confounding and strong feedback loops.
source_refs.author: Joris M. Mooij, Sara Magliacane, Tom Claassen

source_refs.claim: The benchmark uses multiple molecular interventions and single-cell measurements to orient protein-signaling relations.
source_refs.author: Karen Sachs, Omar Perez, Dana Pe'er, Douglas A. Lauffenburger, Garry P. Nolan

source_refs.claim: The paper develops near-optimal confidence intervals for approximate GMM moments by explicitly accounting for bounded misspecification bias.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesár

open_problems.why_unsolved: An exact cumulant-plane formula is brittle to small violations, while the Sachs application is known to contain imperfect interventions, uncertain targets, feedback, and latent confounding. JCI represents these complications graphically but does not provide sharp numerical effect bounds, and approximate-moment GMM theory does not specify how biological deviations map into cumulant-flag violations. The missing link is a perturbation metric connecting off-target or feedback magnitude to feasible cumulant residuals and hence to an effect identified set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified interval for a selected protein effect as a function of explicit cumulant-plane and feedback violation radii, a breakdown radius for point conclusions, and uniformly valid bias-aware confidence sets for the interval endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: Its Sachs discussion directly frames the imperfect-intervention, feedback, and latent-confounding concerns that motivate sensitivity analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Single-cell perturbations offer causal information -> intervention targets and strengths are uncertain -> feedback and latent causes violate idealized acyclic assumptions -> report sharp effect robustness regions rather than exact-model point estimates

method_exemplars.technique: Use its exact mixed-moment equations as the zero-misspecification center and relax each equality into a bounded residual constraint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed identified set should collapse to its higher-moment effect formula when all violation radii vanish.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt bias-aware GMM weighting, modulus calculations, and near-optimal confidence intervals under bounded moment misspecification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Bounded deviations from the cumulant plane generate an approximate moment model with a scalar causal target.

literature_map:
1. Shimizu, Hoyer, Hyvärinen, and Kerminen (JMLR 2006) establish the foundational LiNGAM result that independent non-Gaussian errors identify a linear acyclic model from one observational law.
2. Rothenhäusler, Heinze, Peters, and Meinshausen (NeurIPS 2015, BACKSHIFT) use covariance differences and joint diagonalization to identify cyclic linear systems under unknown shifts, with at least three settings playing a sharp role.
3. Peters, Bühlmann, and Meinshausen (JRSSB 2016) derive invariant causal prediction across heterogeneous environments but require interventions rich enough to distinguish candidate causes.
4. Rothenhäusler, Bühlmann, and Meinshausen (Annals of Statistics 2019, Causal Dantzig) exploit inner-product invariance under additive interventions with hidden variables and derive regular intervals; weak interventions inflate variance.
5. Huang et al. (JMLR 2020) study heterogeneous and nonstationary causal discovery and show that pooling shifted mechanisms can create residual dependence.
6. Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (JMLR 2020, JCI) model multiple unknown intervention types and emphasize that Sachs data contain imperfect interventions, likely latent confounding, and feedback.
7. Cai, Huang, Chen, Hao, and Zhang (ICML 2023) derive higher-cumulant recovery for latent-variable LiNGAM, including one-latent closed forms and iterative removal for multiple latent components.
8. Long, Zhu, Do, and Ha (Electronic Journal of Statistics 2023) recast Causal Dantzig as GMM, optimally combine environments, derive regular asymptotics, and apply it to flow cytometry.
9. Chen, Li, Shen, and Pan (JASA 2024, GrIVET) combine network discovery and likelihood inference with hidden confounding and uncertain multi-target interventions, but rely on Gaussian instrumental-variable structure.
10. Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (La Matematica 2025) use coupled higher-order cumulant tensors across contexts for linear causal disentanglement under restricted latent interventions.
11. Tramontano et al. (ICML 2025) identify latent-variable LiNGAM effects from higher-order cumulants with a proxy or underspecified instrument, showing that cumulants can replace some auxiliary-variable richness.
12. Kivva, Akbari, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (UAI 2025) are the closest anchor: they identify effects under one changing mechanism, prove failure when latent and treatment noises both shift across two environments, and leave joint multi-environment rescue open.
13. Andrews (Quantitative Economics 2019) supplies singularity-robust weak-identification inference, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (Annals of Statistics 2013) supply simultaneous Gaussian and bootstrap calibration; neither treats cumulant moments containing an estimated spectral projector.
14. Sachs et al. (Science 2005) remain the motivating multi-environment protein-signaling application, but later analyses show intervention specificity, feedback, and latent sufficiency are substantive concerns.
prior_proposal_map:
The available research catalogue contained no bank directory, bank README, writeup, or rejected-angle archive.
The only proposal-like core was an interrupted v1 artifact for stat_pomdp_latent_overlap_minimax.
Its honest scope yielded POMDP questions about shrinking overlap and bounded hidden-state cardinality, which were mathematically specific but unrelated to the present cumulant-shift topic and were dropped during topic-sensitive quality filtering.
Its technical limitation yielded a stationary observed-filtration KL bottleneck, also unrelated to the topic.
The panel_ipcw_spectral_ssc_inference mathematical review yielded primitive total-variation learner-rate and transport-assumption questions, both outside the topic anchor.
The pid_recurrent_capacity_transport_regret review passed without findings and yielded no opportunity.
No prior proposal in the available tree directly concerned environmental cumulant flags, simultaneous source shifts, estimated cumulant subspaces, or the Sachs protein-signaling application.
Consequently, cross-track comparison produced no same-opportunity or same-paper matches and no source=both entries.
